{{2025–26 Big 12 men's basketball standings}}
The '''2025–26 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arizona]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by [[Tommy Lloyd]] in his fifth season as head coach. The season marked the Wildcats' 52nd season at [[McKale Center]] in [[Tucson, Arizona]], and their second season as members of the [[Big 12 Conference men's basketball|Big 12 Conference]].

Arizona won their first Big 12 regular season title and 30th regular season conference title in school history.<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 2 Arizona Captures Big 12 Regular Season Title With Win Over Iowa State, 73-57 |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2026/3/2/mens-basketball-no-2-arizona-captures-big-12-regular-season-title-with-win-over-iowa-state-73-57.aspx#:~:text=%E2%80%94%20No.%202%20Arizona%20clinched%20the,those%20being%20regular%20season%20titles.}}</ref> They are also the first Arizona team to have 29 regular season wins, and have the most wins in a season, with 36. The Arizona Wildcats drew an average home attendance of 14,297, the 15th-highest of all college basketball teams.

==Previous season==
{{main|2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team}}

The [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] 24–13, 14–6 in [[2024–25 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 Conference]] play, finishing tied for third and received the number 3 seed in the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]]. They lost to number 1 seed [[2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the finals 72–64.<ref>{{cite web |title=Uzan Scores 25 Points, No. 2 Houston Beats Arizona 72-64 for the Phillips 66 Big 12 MBB Championship Title |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2025/3/16/mens-basketball-uzan-scores-25-points-no-2-houston-beats-arizona-72-64-for-the-phillips-66-big-12-mbb-championship-title.aspx}}</ref> The Wildcats were invited to their 35th [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance, receiving the number 4 seed in the East Regional. They lost in the Sweet Sixteen to number 1 seed [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Flagg flies in March Madness and Duke wins 100-93 over Arizona to reach the Elite Eight |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401746061/arizona-duke}}</ref>

==Offseason==

===Coaching staff changes===

Former assistant coach [[Steve Robinson (basketball)|Steve Robinson]] announced his retirement following a 42-year long coaching career. He held jobs previously at [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] as the head coach, as well as [[Radford Highlanders men's basketball|Radford]], [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Steve Robinson Announces Retirement After 42-Year Coaching Career |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2025/4/24/mens-basketball-steve-robinson-announces-retirement-after-42-year-coaching-career.aspx}}</ref> On May 5, 2025, Arizona hired former [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] assistant coach Brandon Chappell as the replacement for Robinson. Chappell spent the previous three seasons with Texas as an assistant, as well as assistant coach with [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]], [[Lamar Cardinals basketball|Lamar]] (his alma mater) [[Arkansas–Fort Smith Lions|Arkansas-Fort Smith]] and [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona]] as a graduate assistant under current associate head coach Murphy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chappell Joins Arizona Men’s Basketball Staff As Assistant Coach |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2025/5/5/mens-basketball-chappell-joins-arizona-mens-basketball-staff-as-assistant-coach.aspx}}</ref> On August 1, 2025 Rem Bakamus took an assistant coaching position with [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=McCasland adds Bakamus, Bacon to coaching staff |url=https://texastech.com/news/2025/8/1/mens-basketball-mccasland-adds-bakamus-bacon-to-coaching-staff}}</ref> On September 4, 2025 Arizona promoted Evan Manning to assistant coach and hired Austin Torres as director of basketball operations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Men’s Basketball Promotes Manning to Assistant Coach; Torres Returns as Director of Basketball Operations |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2025/9/4/mens-basketball-arizona-mens-basketball-promotes-manning-to-assistant-coach-torres-returns-as-director-of-basketball-operations.aspx}}</ref>

=== Red and Blue game ===
Arizona played its annual Red Blue game on October 3, 2025. The team was split into two teams, Red and Blue and proceeded to play an inter-squad scrimmage. The night featured a basketball game with Arizona's Adaptive Athletics wheelchair basketball team, a three-point contest that had two members of the men's team: [[Anthony Dell'Orso]] and <dfn>Evan Nelson</dfn> <dfn>and two members of the [[2025–26 Arizona Wildcats women's basketball team|Arizona women's team]]: Mickayla Perdue and Mireia Jurado and a dunk contest featuring four members of the men's team: Dwayne Aristode, Mabil Mawut, Addison Arnold, and [[Koa Peat]].</dfn>

The three point contest was won won by Dell'Orso, who defeated Perdue of the women's team, 19−18 in the final round. The dunk contest was judged by Hannah Fields, Myles O'Neal, [[Rob Gronkowski]], [[Mix Master Mike]], and [[Camille Kostek]]. The two final contestants of the dunk contest were <dfn>Aristode</dfn> and <dfn>Arnold but the dunk contest was won by Gronkowski who jumped over a [[Power Wheels|power wheel car]], with all the judges giving him a ten for a combined score of fifty.</dfn>

In the inter-squad scrimmage the Red team, which was coached by assistant coach TJ Benson defeated the Blue team 45−44, which was coached by assistant coach Ken Nakagawa. [[Brayden Burries]], who played on the Red team, led all scoring with twenty-two points, four players: Dell'Orso (Blue), [[Motiejus Krivas]] (Blue), Burries (Red) and [[Tobe Awaka]] (Red) had five rebounds, and Jaden Bradley led both teams in assists with four. Gronkowski, snuck onto the court to play with the Blue team wearing a wig, fake mustache and jersey with the name "Rocky Gronkstone", but was ejected by the officials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Red Team Wins Red-Blue Showcase; Dell'Orso, Gronkowski Win Competitions |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2025/10/3/mens-basketball-red-team-wins-red-blue-showcase-dell-orso-gronkowski-win-competitions.aspx}}</ref>
